How we can help

Every client starts somewhere different: an idea that needs shaping, a project that needs funding, a policy issue to work through, or partners who need to come together. We meet you where you are.

Strategy & Advice

We help you think through difficult issues and decide what to do next, from shaping an early idea to strengthening a business case, assessing risk or understanding why an initiative has stalled. We also advise leaders who want an experienced outside perspective.

Government & Policy

We know how decisions get made, how policy develops and how programs and funding work. We help organizations engage government effectively, and we help governments develop policy and programs across departments and jurisdictions.

Partnerships & Facilitation

Important work depends on people who don’t normally work together. We build partnerships and coalitions and design workshops that end with clarity: who will do what, and what happens next.

Knowledge Mobilization

Good research often sits on shelves. We turn research, data and practitioner experience into briefings, roadmaps, frameworks and tools that people can actually use.

Projects & Financing

Strong projects stall when the funding or the business case isn’t there. We help build the case, identify funding and partners, work through risks, and bring public funding and private capital together, especially for infrastructure and resilience.

Bring us the challenge

Climate & resilience

Climate change is reshaping the communities, infrastructure and systems we depend on. Responding takes two things at once: reducing the emissions that drive it, and preparing for the impacts already on the way.

Reducing emissions

The shift to lower emissions is now an energy, technology, industrial and investment transition. Lo has helped shape it: contributing to international methods for estimating greenhouse gas emissions, helping establish Canada’s industrial greenhouse gas reporting system, developing approaches to carbon markets and offsets, and representing Canada in international climate negotiations.

Building resilience

Lo created and led the Canadian Centre for Climate Services, helped establish ClimateWest and CLIMAtlantic, led the infrastructure work for Canada’s first National Adaptation Strategy, helped develop the Climate Lens for federal infrastructure investments, and served on the Green Municipal Fund Council and Investment Committee.

Reducing risk at scale takes many measures working together, from natural infrastructure and stormwater systems to land-use decisions, insurance and emergency preparedness. It also pays off: the Canadian Climate Institute estimates that prevention and resilience investments can return up to $15 in avoided losses and other benefits for every dollar spent.

We know enough to act.

The tools, technology and evidence exist. What’s needed now is scale: deploying proven solutions, upgrading infrastructure, using natural systems to reduce risk and bringing strong projects forward. The results are tangible: lower emissions, homes better protected from floods and wildfire, infrastructure that performs in a changing climate, and communities better prepared.

Implementation is the function. Community wellbeing is the purpose.

The meaning behind the name

សុខ Sokha

In Khmer, Sokha speaks to health, happiness and peaceful wellbeing. Rooted in founder Lo Cheng’s Cambodian heritage, it carries a simple wish: for people and communities to be well, not merely to endure but to thrive.

North reflects our Canadian roots and a sense of direction. Much of our work involves complexity, with different interests and institutions and often no obvious path forward. North speaks to knowing what you are working toward.

Together, Sokha North means wellbeing and direction: a name grounded in purpose, place and a clear sense of what matters.

Deep expertise. Trusted judgement.

I’m an environmental engineer by training, and I’ve spent more than 25 years working on complex public-interest challenges across the public and private sectors, in climate, infrastructure, environmental policy, regulation, finance and emergency management. I’ve negotiated internationally and with industry, built new organizations and programs, governed major investments and responded to environmental emergencies.

What I’ve learned is that complex problems rarely sit neatly within one organization, discipline or mandate. I look across those boundaries, connecting policy with finance, evidence with decisions, and institutions with the communities they serve. Often the most interesting possibilities emerge in the connections.

After more than two decades in the federal public service, I created Sokha North to focus those experiences on work where I can make a meaningful contribution.

I hold an Executive MBA from Queen’s University and a Bachelor of Engineering in Environmental Engineering from Carleton University.

Family has always been central to my life, and my definition of it has never been limited by geography or blood. I love bringing people together, usually around a table and always with more food than necessary. Please let me feed you. Outside of work, I’m usually outdoors, biking, kayaking or cross-country skiing.
